Found the pattern in memory — this is the third time (Aug 11, Aug 19, now Sep 3), and the pieces line up into one root cause:

- The atlas CI pipeline auto-cancels any job still running past **30 minutes**.
- Every release build starts with an **empty cargo registry cache** (no persistent caching configured).
- A cold cargo registry cache alone adds **~18 minutes** to the build.

So the release build has almost no margin: cold-cache overhead eats over half the 30-minute budget before compilation even starts, and any normal variance (dependency changes, slower runner, etc.) pushes it over the line and CI kills it. It's not flaky — it's structurally timing out.

Fix options, in order of preference:
1. **Cache the cargo registry** between release builds (e.g. `actions/cache` keyed on `Cargo.lock`) — removes the ~18 min tax entirely.
2. If caching isn't feasible, raise the job timeout past 30 minutes to give it headroom.

Both are cheap; #1 is the real fix since it also speeds up every build, not just keeps it under the wire.

I've saved this root cause to memory so it surfaces automatically next time instead of needing to be re-derived. Want me to look at the atlas CI config and actually wire up the cargo cache?
